title: refactor(transformer): Move TransformCtx into TraverseCtx state to eliminate RefCells
body_preview:
## Problem

The transformer currently uses `TransformCtx` which contains shared state between all transforms, stored as immutable references `&'ctx TransformCtx<'a>` in each transformer. This design forces all mutable state to be wrapped in `RefCell`s (e.g., the shared `VarDeclarations` stack), which adds runtime overhead and makes the code less ergonomic.

## Solution

This PR implements the architectural change proposed in #11742 by moving all fields from `TransformCtx` into `TransformState`, which becomes the generic parameter `T` of `TraverseCtx<'a, T>`. Since `TraverseCtx` is passed as `&mut TraverseCtx<'a, T>` to every visitor method, transformers now have mutable access to shared state through `ctx.state`, eliminating the need for `RefCell` wrappers.

## Key Changes

### Architecture
- **Moved all fields** from `TransformCtx` to `TransformState` (errors, helper_loader, module_imports, var_declarations, etc.)
- **Updated type alias**: `TraverseCtx<'a> = oxc_traverse::TraverseCtx<'a, TransformState<'a>>`

title: [ServiceBus] Consider retry attempts with ServerBusy exit logic
body_preview:
## Summary

Updates the ServiceBusRetryPolicy ServerBusy exit logic to consider the total time available across all remaining retry attempts, rather than just the single attempt timeout.

## Problem

The current implementation exits early when `IsServerBusy && tryTimeout < ServerBusyBaseSleepTime` (10 seconds), without considering that multiple retry attempts could provide sufficient total time for the operation to succeed.

**Example scenario:**
- Single attempt timeout: 5 seconds
- Max retries: 3
- ServerBusy sleep time: 10 seconds
- **Current behavior**: Exit early because 5s < 10s
- **Expected behavior**: Proceed because total time (5s × 3 = 15s) > 10s

## Solution

Modified the ServerBusy condition to use:
```csharp
(tryTimeout * (GetMaxRetries() - failedAttemptCount)) < ServerBusyBaseSleepTime
```

This considers the time available across all remaining retry attempts when deciding whether to exit early.

title: log: replace SyncHandler with AsyncStreamHandler to fix goroutine contention
body_preview:
## Problem

Under heavy validator load (thousands of Caplin validator goroutines logging
concurrently), all goroutines serialised on the `sync.Mutex` inside
`SyncHandler`. This caused complete process freezes on the Caplin beacon API
— a goroutine dump showed 8 295 of 9 875 goroutines blocked on the same mutex
address waiting for a log write.

## Solution

Add `AsyncHandler` and `AsyncStreamHandler` to `common/log/v3`:

- **`AsyncHandler(bufSize, h)`** — wraps any `Handler` with a buffered
  channel (`asyncDefaultBufSize = 4096`). Callers enqueue via
  `select { case h.recs <- r: default: h.dropped.Add(1) }` — they **never
  block** even when the channel is full. A single drain goroutine writes
  records sequentially, eliminating the shared mutex. Dropped records are
  counted atomically and reported as a `Warn` entry after each batch.

- **`AsyncStreamHandler(wr, fmtr)`** — convenience constructor:
  `LazyHandler(AsyncHandler(asyncDefaultBufSize, streamHandler{wr, fmtr}))`.
  `LazyHandler` is outermost so `Lazy` values are evaluated in the caller's
  goroutine, not the drain goroutine.

Switch the predefined handlers and logging setup:
- `StdoutHandler` / `StderrHandler` in `root.go` → `AsyncStreamHandler`
- Both `StreamHandler` usages in `node/logging/logging.go` → `AsyncStreamHandler`

`SyncHandler` is preserved unchanged for tests and any synchronous pipelines

title: Add `UnwrapIfPromiseAsync` extension method for non-blocking promise resolution
body_preview:
`UnwrapIfPromise` blocks the calling thread while waiting for a `JsPromise` to settle, which causes thread pool exhaustion in async .NET environments. `EvaluateAsync`/`InvokeAsync` cover the common cases, but there's no async path when you already hold a `JsValue` that may be a promise (e.g., from `Call()`, `GetValue()`, etc.).

## Changes

- **`Engine.Async.cs`**: `UnwrapResultAsync` promoted from `private` to `internal` to allow delegation from extension methods.
- **`JsValueExtensions.cs`**: New `UnwrapIfPromiseAsync(this JsValue, CancellationToken = default)` extension — delegates to `promise.Engine.UnwrapResultAsync` for promises, short-circuits with `Task.FromResult` for non-promise values.
- **`README.md`**: Added a new "Asynchronous Execution" section documenting `EvaluateAsync`/`ExecuteAsync`/`InvokeAsync` and `UnwrapIfPromiseAsync` with code examples and guidance on when to use each.

## Usage

```csharp
// Blocking (old):
var result = engine.Invoke("fetchData", url).UnwrapIfPromise();

// Non-blocking (new):
var result = await engine.Invoke("fetchData", url).UnwrapIfPromiseAsync(cancellationToken);
```

Respects `Options.Constraints.PromiseTimeout` and cancellation, matching the behaviour of `EvaluateAsync`.

title: Optimize Network.Check single-IP path to reduce allocations
body_preview:
`Network.Check` called `extractIP` on every event value, unconditionally allocating a `[]net.IP` slice even for the dominant single-IP case. This adds ~40 B and 2 allocs per op on a hot path.

**Changes:**
- Replace `extractIP` + `slices.ContainsFunc` with a type switch in `Check` that fast-paths `string` and `net.IP` without slice construction
- Add `containsAny`/`containsAnyStr` helpers for `[]net.IP` and `[]string` slice cases
- Remove now-unused `extractIP` function and `slices` import

```go
// Before: always allocates []net.IP
ipList := extractIP(value)
if !slices.ContainsFunc(ipList, network.Contains) { ... }

// After: no allocation for single-IP types
switch v := value.(type) {
case string:
    ip := net.ParseIP(v)
    if ip == nil || !network.Contains(ip) { return false }
case net.IP:
    if !network.Contains(v) { return false }
case []net.IP:
    if len(v) == 0 || !containsAny(v, network.Contains) { return false }
case []string:
    if len(v) == 0 || !containsAnyStr(v, network.Contains) { return false }
}
```

**Benchmark (10 runs):** ~181 → ~139 ns/op, 40 → 16 B/op, 2 → 1 allocs/op.

title: Prevent deadlock in benchlist using dedicated notification worker goroutine
body_preview:
## Why this should be merged

The `run()` goroutine's synchronous calls to `Benched()` and `Unbenched()` can deadlock if the `Benchable` implementation blocks on a channel whose consumer is waiting to send to the benchlist's `jobs` channel.

## How this works

Instead of spawning a goroutine for every notification, this implementation uses a single dedicated worker goroutine pattern:

1. **Notification Channel**: Added a buffered `notifications` channel (same size as `jobs` channel)
2. **Worker Goroutine**: A single `processNotifications()` worker consumes from this channel and makes the actual `Benched()`/`Unbenched()` calls
3. **Non-blocking Sends**: The `run()` loop uses a `sendNotification()` helper that performs non-blocking sends via select statement
4. **Graceful Degradation**: If the notification buffer is full, notifications are dropped with warning logs to prevent blocking

State management (`benched` set, `timeoutHeap`) remains synchronous before sending notifications, maintaining consistency while preventing blocking.

```go
// Before: synchronous call that could block
b.benchable.Unbenched(b.ctx.ChainID, nodeID)

// After: non-blocking dispatch through dedicated worker
b.sendNotification(job{nodeID: nodeID, bench: false})
```

This approach is more efficient than spawning goroutines per notification and maintains notification ordering through the channel.

On Linux, `System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection` does not honor the `Timeout` property at the network layer, causing network operations (such as connect or bind) to potentially hang indefinitely or much longer than the requested timeout. body_preview:

title: Merge compatible variable modifications in CometAdapter for improved performance
body_preview:
Comet runs 3x+ slower when modifications with the same mass are specified as separate entries (e.g., `Carbamyl (K)`, `Carbamyl (R)`) instead of merged (`KR`). This also unnecessarily consumes the 9-entry modification limit.

## Changes

- **Added `CometModification` struct** to represent and merge Comet variable modification entries
  - `isMergeableWith()` - checks mass equality, binary group, and terminal compatibility
  - `merge()` - combines residues, preserves terminal specificity
  - `toCometString()` - generates Comet param format

- **Merging rules**:
  - Same mass (within 1e-6) and binary group required
  - Protein terminal mods (nc_term 0,1) kept separate
  - Peptide N-term and C-term cannot merge together
  - Peptide terminal + amino acid mods can merge

- **Error handling**: 9-entry limit now checked after merging

## Example

Before:
```
variable_mod01 = 43.0058 K 0 5 -1 0 0 0.0
variable_mod02 = 43.0058 R 0 5 -1 0 0 0.0
variable_mod03 = 43.0058 S 0 5 -1 0 0 0.0
```

After:
```
variable_mod01 = 43.0058 KRS 0 5 -1 0 0 0.0
```

Fixes #6203

title: fix: suppress incomplete provider lock file warning for ephemeral workdirs
body_preview:
When Atmos manages the plugin cache (`TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`), Terraform emits a noisy warning about incomplete lock file checksums on every `init` against an ephemeral workdir — which is every run, since workdirs are recreated fresh each time and never retain a `.terraform.lock.hcl`.

A prior fix attempted to suppress the warning by disabling the plugin cache when no lock file exists, which backfired: it eliminated the cache benefit precisely when providers need to be installed.

## Approach

Two separate strategies by directory type:

- **Workdir mode** (`WorkdirPathKey` set by the workdir provisioner): cache stays fully enabled; the Terraform warning is suppressed at the I/O layer via a new stderr filter. The lock file is disposable by design, so the warning is genuinely non-actionable.
- **Non-workdir JIT source mode**: retain the existing `buildInitEnvList` behavior — disable the Atmos-managed cache on first `init` (no lock file → providers fetched from registry with `h1:` checksums), re-enable once the lock file exists.

title: [MPS] Reimplement torch.linalg.cross as a native Metal kernel
body_preview:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.14.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #175499

Replace the old `generateKernelDataOffsets`-based implementation with
dense and strided kernel flavors. The dense path handles all contiguous
tensors (outermost, innermost, or any cross-dim position) via a
closed-form index mapping `base = tid + 2*(tid/B)*B` where B is the
cross-dim element stride; the strided path covers non-contiguous inputs
using squashed sizes and full per-tensor element strides with the
cross-dim stride looked up by index. Complex types (ComplexFloat,
ComplexHalf) are supported via `c10::metal::mul`. Benchmarking showed
no measurable gain from Metal's built-in `cross()` function, so the
generic template is used throughout.
